messages:
sam: Quick q—for the new inference-config service: do we expose gRPC+protobuf internally and let gateways transcode, or expose JSON REST from the gateway and keep clients simple?

maria: My 2¢: gRPC gives better perf and typed contracts; but we already have a lot of JS clients that hate binary/proto parsing.

devon: Agree on types. But gateway-transcoding means we lose clear error codes and miss some telemetry granularity unless we propagate metadata.

alex: Related: quotas + routing policies are enforced at the gateway. If we do proto behind gateway we need to decide where quota attribution happens — on gateway or on backend.

jordan: We should pick based on rollout UX. If gateway does transcode, console shows REST endpoints to product teams. If backend stays typed we need generated client libs surfaced in console.

maria: Telemetry note — with gRPC we can stream request-level metadata (peer, kv cache hits) in trailers. Transcoding can swallow that unless we copy headers.

devon: For canary and fallbacks I'd prefer typed backend + gateway shim that translates. Easy to fallback to JSON-only backend variant when capacity is low.

sam: Example shim config idea:

```
gateway:
  routes:
    - path: /v1/infer
      to: inference-service.internal.svc:grpc
      transcode: true
      propagate_headers: [x-tenant, x-request-id, x-client-proto]
      quota_key: "x-tenant"
```

alex: That helps. But we need to ensure quota enforcement sees consistent tokens. If gateway enforces quotas, backend shouldn't re-check; else double-billing risk.

jordan: UX: If we expose typed surfaces in Console we should auto-generate SDKs and docs. Otherwise product teams will copy/paste fragile REST shapes.

maria: Ops question — do we prefer sidecar approach (each pod has tiny json <-> proto adapter) or single shared gateway translator? Sidecar gives locality and avoids cross-gateway fanout, but more deployment complexity.

devon: Sidecar simplifies telemetry correlation (trace spans inside pod) but complicates rolling upgrades across services.

sam: Can we agree on a middle ground? - typed backend (gRPC/proto) for service-to-service; shared gateway that transcodes for external clients; and a small sidecar option for lat-critical paths.

alex: Sounds pragmatic. Actionables:
- Document header propagation contract (maria)
- Telemetry mapping spec for transcode (devon)
- Console SDK generation prototype (jordan)
- Quota ownership doc: gateway vs backend (sam)

jordan: I'll sketch the console mock for generated SDKs and include a toggle to expose either REST docs or proto SDKs per route.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway-transcode-proto-skim v0.1 -> canary at 2025-11-02T09:00Z :rocket:

maria: Thanks — will start a PR with header list and propagate test harness. Small follow-up: anyone strongly opposed to this hybrid? If not I'll start writing the spec.

alex: No strong objections from me.

devon: +1

sam: +1

jordan: +1

maria: Great — I'll open the RFC and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:
